title: Tenants march in Madrid and 50 Spanish cities over rents and evictions
seoTitle: Madrid housing protests over rents, evictions

tea.why: Rents have soared and an 87-year-old tenant was evicted after her investor landlord raised the rent from €500 to €1,650.
tea.want: Stop evictions of vulnerable tenants, curb investment funds and short-term lets, and automatically renew leases.
tea.changed: Oct 5: PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for Nov 29 after parliament rejected his housing decrees.

summary: Housing protests have spread across Spain since the September 23 eviction of an 87-year-old woman from the Madrid flat she had rented for about seven decades, after an investment firm raised her rent. Tenants' groups set up a protest camp in central Madrid and held noisy 'cacerolada' protests outside city halls ahead of a parliamentary vote. On October 2 Congress rejected two government decrees to limit evictions, restrict short-term lets and renew leases automatically, as hundreds protested outside. On October 3 marches were held in about 50 cities; the Spanish government put the Madrid turnout at around 70,000, while the organising Tenants' Union claimed 500,000. Some marchers called for a general strike. On October 5 Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early general election for November 29, saying he needed a broader majority to pass housing reforms. The eviction itself was later reversed by the building's owner.
demands: Tighter limits on short-term and seasonal lets
Some marchers called for a general strike
response: Parliament rejected the government's two housing decrees on Oct 2; PM Pedro Sánchez then called a snap election for Nov 29.

crowd.text: around 70,000 in Madrid on Oct 3, according to the government; organisers claimed 500,000

updates.text: An 87-year-old tenant was evicted in Madrid after her rent was raised; protests followed outside the building.
Several hundred people banged pots outside Madrid city hall and other town halls ahead of the vote.
Congress rejected both housing decrees as hundreds protested outside parliament.
Marches in about 50 cities; four columns converged on Madrid's Cibeles Square.
PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for Nov 29.
